note: Establish a C5/C6 feed split and measure product distributions and column cost before adding downstream columns.
notebook: PLAN: First split C5-and-lighter from C6-and-heavier, then recover high-value C5/C6 products and blends while measuring costs; add only separations with clear payback. Step 1: characterize the feed split. Initial 45-stage column at 14.4 bar with R=B=3, aiming tops through n-pentane and bottoms from 2,2-dimethylbutane. Later consider pressure optimization, side draws, and selling easy C3/C4/C5 blends instead of expensive pure-product polishing.

note: Test a three-column blend train producing C3, C4, and C5 products, with a stronger C5/C6 split.
notebook: PLAN: Build a blend-based light-ends train first (C3, C4, C5), then add C6 paraffin/naphthene and C7+ recovery only where revenue exceeds column cost. Step 2: test three sharp splits: feed C4-/C5+, tops C3/C4, bottoms C5/C6+. Initial feed column at 14.4 bar, R=B=3 gave a C5/C6 cut with about 65 mol/s C6 leakage and incomplete C5 recovery. Blends should beat difficult pure-product polishing: estimated revenues C3 $59M, C4 $174M, C5 $610M, C6 paraffin $1091M, C6 naphthene $393M/yr. Current test uses a moderate C3/C4 column and a stronger 55-stage C5/C6 split because that boiling gap is only ~13 K.

note: Sharpen the C5 blend and C6-paraffin blend cuts; these two products should create substantial revenue immediately.
notebook: PLAN: Establish three blend cuts: C4-/C5+ at root, C4-/C5 in tops, and C5/C6+ in bottoms. Then split the resulting C6+ into paraffin and naphthene blends and C7+ products if profitable. Step 3: sharpen all three splits enough to generate the first revenue. Prior root split at R=B=3 leaked C6 into tops; B split at R=B=4 left 21% N-pentane in BT. Blend targets are worth roughly C5 $610M/yr and C6 paraffin $1091M/yr, so high reflux on these key columns is justified initially. Remove or repurpose unprofitable light-end polishing after revenue appears.

note: Sharpen the C4/C5 and C5/C6 splits aggressively to get the two high-value blends above 95% and establish whether this architecture can be profitable.

Using unequal reflux/boil-up should move each cut to the desired flow rather than merely adding expensive stages. Step: test 70/3/8 root and 80/4/10 B, then tune purity and costs.
